I just got done with CS50P and created a program that analyzes nouns in Akkadian (the language of Babylon) as well as a small game. I've tried learning to code about 8 years ago when I was 13 with learnpython, but was stuck in tutorial Hell. Earlier this year, I tried Python Crash Course, and found the pace far too slow and the assignments far too easy. CS50P was the first that challenged me and broke me out of my comfort zone, and I'm grateful equally to Malan and the team behind CS50 in general. I plan on pursuing CS50AI to learn more about applied ML (as I'd like to go into computational linguistics), CS50 2D for gamedev in Lua (when it comes out) and CS50x as well down the line. The fact of the matter is, CS50P equipped me with a new mindset: not syntax memorization, but linguistic fluency in Python. Just like learning a language, you don't memorize phrases, you keep rules in mind and make novel sentences of your own. Python is very much the same. It doesn't matter how much syntax you know if you can't express an idea of your own. And CS50 truly does give that to you. Thank you Malan, thank you CS50, thank you Harvard. Just more proof that the Internet can really be a modern London coffeehouse.
